title: Sewer deaths and the official manual scavenging count
summary: Union replies publish hundreds of sanitation-worker deaths from hazardous sewer and septic-tank cleaning since 2019 (NCSK), while often reporting zero deaths due to manual scavenging under the same Act. Check year-wise and state-wise death and compensation figures, NAMASTE delivery numbers, and successive Lok Sabha or PIB answers for consistency against the PEMSA 2013 definitions and the scheme's stated zero-fatality aim.
authority: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK)
scope: Year-wise and state-wise NCSK-reported deaths from hazardous sewer and septic-tank cleaning in successive Union replies since 2019
Compensation paid, partial, and not-confirmed counts versus reported deaths in the same annexures
NAMASTE scheme delivery metrics (validated SSWs, PPE kits, ERSU safety devices, health cards) versus the stated zero-fatality aim
How successive official replies apply PEMSA 2013 definitions of manual scavenging versus hazardous cleaning
out_of_scope: Naming or profiling of workers, families, or contractors
statutory_anchors: Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 — Section 7 (hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks)
PEMSA 2013 Section 2 definitions of manual scavenger and hazardous cleaning
